blocks.text: Individuals associated with this lifestyle often showcase their affluence through social media, featuring expensive possessions, travel, and experiences. There is an emphasis on self-care, high-end cosmetics, and luxury goods. The term carries both positive connotations, reflecting aspiration and achievement, and negative connotations, highlighting perceived materialism or detachment from social issues.

Boujee is related to the New Money concept, emphasizing overt displays of wealth, in contrast to the more understated Old Money aesthetic. Confidence, a focus on personal enjoyment, and a degree of perceived entitlement are often associated with the "boujee" lifestyle.
Visuals are very decadent, fancy, and over-the-top, showing off things like luxury brand, high-end fashion, expensive jewelry, etc.
Expensive designer clothing, accessories and shoes
Brands like Gucci, Chanel, Louis Vuitton and Balenciaga
Glammed-up, glitzy makeup such dramatically done eyelashes, perfectly contoured cheek and glossed or matte lips in rich natural or gold colors
Gold chains, diamond-encrusted accessories, rings with embedded with jewels, luxury watches like Rolex, fancy expensive bracelets, necklaces and arm bands
Expensive wines and champagnes in wine glass and champagne flutes
Fine dining and gourmet cuisine like steak, salmon, oysters, caviar and lobster

Exotic animals (note: if you plan to get an exotic animal, please do TONS of research before doing so and evaluate if your current environment is suitable for the animal and if you're able to care for it. Plus, exotic animals are NOT domesticated so they will be messy, loud, expensive and require specialized vets, groomers, etc. Keep in mind owning certain exotic animals may also be illegal depending where you live.)
Brand-new smartphones of the latest lines

Boujee fashion is very extravagant, over-the-top, and flashy, with huge name brands being very popular, such as Hermes, Gucci, Chanel, Armani, Alexander McQueen, Louis Vuitton, Dior, Cartier, Versace, BOSS, Tom Ford, etc. The Boujee fashion can trace its roots back to the Haute Couture (French for "high dressmaking") fashion genre, the creation of exclusive custom-fitted clothing first started in the 1800s. It is high-end fashion that is constructed by hand from start to finish, made from high-quality, expensive, often unusual fabric and sewn with extreme attention to detail and finished by the most experienced and capable sewers, often using time-consuming, hand-executed techniques.
Boujee fashion also tends to be chic, elegant, and stylish way that’s associated with a fashionable lifestyle, ideology, or pursuit wearing the latest. Fashion items for the ladies can include:
Big curls, or super flat ironed hair
As far as make-up goes, Boujee make also tends to be very extravagant, bold, and over-the-top with noticeable fake lashes. Reversley, Boujee people can also be masters of the "no-makeup" makeup look.

For the men, there is Evening Black Tie dress code; a semi-formal Western dress code for evening events, originating in British and American conventions for attire in the 19th century. In British English, the dress code is often referred to synecdochically by its principal element for men, the dinner suit or dinner jacket(sometimes abbreviated to just a DJ). This dress code includes:
A black low-cut waistcoat or a cummerbund.
A white dress, cuffs and a turndown collar.
A black silk bow tie matching the lapel facings
A black evening waistcoat or cummerbund.
Black dress socks, usually of silk or fine wool.
Black shoes, traditionally patent leather court shoes (pumps).

Boujee music covers a range of genres that evoke feelings of living a high-end lifestyle full of opulence and luxury. Most music lyrics are about enjoying the finer things in life and a luxurious life. Despite this, some followers to the Boujee aesthetic might also listen to Lo-Fi music.
Some examples of music artists for the Boujee aesthetic
Hip-Hop and Rap: Artists like Jay-Z, Ye, Drake and Cardi B are known for their music about confidence, living in luxury and plenty of glamor.
R&B and Soul: Artists like Beyoncé, Alicia Keys, Frank Ocean and The Weeknd often sing of luxury and enjoying life's pleasures in their songs.
Pop and Dance-Pop: Artists like Rihanna, Lady Gaga, Ariana Grande and Dua Lipa have tracks that embody the themes glamour, glitz and grandeur of the Boujee lifestyle.
Electronic and EDM: Artists like Calvin Harris, David Guetta, Marshmello and Martin Garrix have songs that embody the nightlife and high-end partying of the Boujee aesthetic.

Jazz and Swing: Artists like Ella Fitzgerald, Louis Armstrong, Duke Ellington and Michael Bublé have plenty of elegant-sounding music that fit with the themes of opulence and glamour of the Boujee aesthetic.
